If the request is made with an array-valued param (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), Rails yields an Array and `split` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 4xx. The frontend sends a comma-joined string, so this only manifests via direct API calls with malformed params — a robustness defect but the mechanism is correctly described and the code is new in this diff. Confidence is moderate because the normal client path never triggers it.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If `usernames` is submitted as an Array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `split` is undefined and will raise `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The diff adds this new endpoint and does not normalize/validate the param type before calling `split`.
